subject.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel

question: Should OpenClaw permanently accept the new generic `toolBindings` run context and paired-browser-origin persistence as the core contract for the bundled browser copilot after the subscription isolation repair?
rationale: The patch is a large feature that crosses browser-plugin ownership, Gateway authentication, event delivery, plugin runtime context, and persisted pairing records; source review can identify the defect but cannot choose the permanent public ownership and compatibility boundary.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
options.body: Approve the generic binding and origin-record seams after broad subscriptions are denied and upgrade behavior is explicitly proven.

options.title: Narrow the contract before merge
options.body: Require the browser plugin to own more of the feature so core exposes only the minimal generic authorization and run-binding seam.

options.title: Pause the feature direction
options.body: Defer the panel until owners choose a different browser/session architecture.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Approve the generic binding and origin-record seams after broad subscriptions are denied and upgrade behavior is explicitly proven.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the proposed cross-surface contract and is the best available routing candidate from the reviewed history.
